answer.text: Fluorescence microscopy images of cells or organelles are frequently corrupted by photon shot noise, dark noise, read noise, and sample-dependent noise because low laser intensities are used to avoid photodamaging live specimens, making densely packed, overlapping objects harder to separate than in clean images.

A robust instance-segmentation network for this domain needs an architecture that both denoises implicitly and reasons globally about which pixels belong to the same object, rather than a plain encoder-decoder that treats a touching-cell cluster as one blob.

I propose a hybrid Attention-Residual U-Net with an optional transformer bottleneck, called AR-TransUNet, trained with a multi-task, multi-loss objective and finished with marker-guided watershed postprocessing.

The encoder replaces plain convolutional blocks with residual blocks, since short residual connections stabilize gradient flow through the layers needed to learn noise-robust filters, while the long, symmetrical encoder-to-decoder skip connections of U-Net preserve fine spatial detail needed to keep thin membrane and organelle boundaries intact.

Each long skip connection passes through an attention gate before concatenation, following the Attention U-Net design in which the gate combines the upsampled decoder feature map with the encoder feature map to produce a soft mask that suppresses background noise while highlighting salient boundaries, the behavior needed when noise surrounds touching cells.

At the bottleneck, a transformer encoder tokenizes the CNN feature map into patches and applies self-attention, following the TransUNet approach of complementing U-Net's local convolutional features with global context, valuable for disambiguating which pixels of a touching cluster belong to which nucleus when local texture alone is ambiguous under noise.

Rather than a single binary output, the decoder ends in three parallel heads, mirroring the contour-aware decomposition used in CA2.5-Net, which splits instance segmentation into a semantic foreground mask, a normal-edge mask, and a clustered-edge mask specifically to handle severely touching nuclei.

A third head regresses horizontal and vertical distance maps from each pixel to its instance centroid, following the HoVer-Net formulation, whose distance regression separates clustered nuclei and yields accurate segmentation even in overlapping regions.

The composite loss combines a class-imbalance term, a regional overlap term, and a contour term: the foreground/background head uses weighted binary cross-entropy or focal loss, since fluorescence images have far more background pixels than object pixels and plain cross-entropy would be dominated by trivially correct background predictions.

A Dice loss rewards regional overlap, and a boundary loss, defined as an integral of predicted softmax probabilities against a precomputed ground-truth distance field, is combined with the Dice term because boundary loss alone has degenerate empty-mask minima and needs the regional loss to dominate early in training while it takes over later.

The edge and distance-map heads reuse the classic U-Net idea of a spatially varying pixel weight w(x), introduced to force the network to learn the thin separating border between touching cells by giving those border pixels disproportionately high weight in the loss.

As a code sketch in plain statements rather than a fenced block: class ResBlock(nn.Module) stacks two 3x3 conv-batchnorm-ReLU layers plus a shortcut summed before the final activation, and class AttentionGate(nn.Module) projects the decoder signal g and encoder skip x to a shared channel count, sums them, applies ReLU then a 1x1 convolution and sigmoid, and multiplies the result onto x before concatenation.

class ARTransUNet(nn.Module) stacks four ResBlock stages with stride-2 downsampling, tokenizes the bottleneck for a small TransformerEncoder, reshapes tokens back to a feature map, and decodes with transposed convolutions, AttentionGate-filtered skips, and three 1x1 heads for the semantic, boundary, and horizontal-vertical distance outputs, trained with total_loss equal to dice_loss plus lambda_focal times focal_loss plus lambda_boundary times boundary_loss(dist_field) plus lambda_hv times mse_loss(hv_pred, hv_gt), with lambda_boundary scheduled to grow across training.

At inference, marker-controlled watershed separates touching objects: seed markers come from local maxima of the denoised intensity image multiplied by the network's foreground detection map, morphological dilation merges maxima too close together to avoid duplicate seeds, and the watershed floods from these markers using the inverted probability or distance surface as the segmentation function so ridge lines fall on the thin borders between cells.

This mirrors the standard recipe of computing a segmentation function, foreground markers, and background markers, then modifying the function so minima occur only at marker locations before flooding, avoiding oversegmentation, an approach also used with a nuclear stain channel seeding markers and a second or inverted-intensity channel defining the flooding surface in fluorescence images.
An additional pruning step analogous to StarDist's non-maximum suppression discards redundant overlapping candidates by thresholding pairwise mask overlap, retaining one instance per true object.

Compared with Cellpose, which represents each cell with a learned vector flow field pushing every pixel toward its cell's center and reliably splits touching cells across microscopy modalities, my model instead predicts distance-to-boundary and horizontal-vertical fields with an attention-gated, noise-suppressing backbone, trading cross-modality generality for stronger denoising and boundary supervision tailored to noisy data.

Compared with StarDist, whose star-convex polygon representation suits round nuclei but constrains object shape and needs a separate probability-and-NMS stage, my model outputs unconstrained pixel-wise masks plus distance maps, better accommodating irregular organelle or cell shapes while still borrowing StarDist's threshold-and-overlap-pruning idea.

Compared with Omnipose, which replaced Cellpose's cell-probability map with a distance field for faster convergence and outperformed both Cellpose and Mask R-CNN on morphologically diverse, touching bacterial cells, my architecture adopts a similar distance-field philosophy but adds attention gating and a transformer bottleneck to exploit global context under heavy sensor noise.

Compared with Mask R-CNN, which proposes regions of interest and predicts a class, box, and mask per region with mask loss defined only for positively matched proposals, my fully convolutional design avoids the region-proposal bottleneck that struggles when many objects are tightly clustered, since dense touching instances are the failure mode proposal-based detectors handle poorly relative to per-pixel distance and boundary regression.

Overall, AR-TransUNet targets the failure modes of noisy fluorescence microscopy with overlapping objects by combining residual and attention mechanisms for noise-robust, boundary-sensitive feature learning, a transformer bottleneck for global disambiguation, a multi-task boundary-and-distance output head, a composite Dice-focal-boundary loss, and marker-controlled watershed postprocessing, positioning it between StarDist's shape-constrained polygons, Cellpose and Omnipose's flow/distance fields, and Mask R-CNN's proposal-based approach.

# AUS research agent

You are a research agent for TREC RAG 2026. Produce a complete,
well-organized, evidence-grounded response using only the available
search/retrieval tools and evidence returned by them. Prior knowledge may help
you choose searches, but it is not evidence and must not support factual claims.

## Scope interpretation

Infer the full deliverable from the entire request, including every concrete
requirement, audience constraint, comparison, example, and requested format.
If light framing such as "overview" or "outline" conflicts with substantial
concrete requirements, the concrete requirements define the real scope.
Resolve ambiguity toward the most complete reasonable interpretation that
stays in scope. Do not ask the user clarifying or confirming questions; proceed
on the strongest reasonable reading.

## Internal success plan

Before the first search, determine internally:

1. **End goal** — one sentence describing what a complete deliverable provides.
2. **Concrete minimum requirements** — the checkable floor that must be met
   before the response is shippable.
3. **Target/excellence requirements** — what a notably strong response adds
   beyond the minimum without expanding scope.
4. **Coverage areas** — the independent topics, claims, comparisons, examples,
   dates, people, mechanisms, or perspectives that require evidence.

Use these requirements to plan searches, track coverage gaps, judge evidence,
and decide when to stop. Do not expose this internal plan unless the requested
answer itself calls for it.

## Research workflow

1. Begin with multiple complementary queries in parallel across independent
   coverage areas.
2. Move from broad discovery to targeted follow-ups for specific names, dates,
   mechanisms, examples, definitions, causal claims, and disputed points.
3. Reformulate weak queries instead of accepting poor coverage. Try synonyms,
   alternative terminology, narrower entities, and different phrasings.
4. Actively search for counter-evidence, contradictions, limitations, and
   missing perspectives when they matter to the request.
5. Continually compare gathered evidence against the minimum and target
   requirements. Search the remaining gaps rather than repeating already
   covered claims.
6. Every tool call must have a concrete purpose tied to an unmet requirement
   or evidence gap. Do not call a tool solely to create another model turn. If
   no meaningful gap remains, write the final report in that same turn.

Search results already contain document text. Inspect that text directly; do
not call another tool merely to fetch the same document. The search tool
normally stages at most about 4,096 tokens per result; request a different
`budget_tokens_per_result` only when a query genuinely needs a different
per-document evidence depth.

## Staged and committed evidence

Every retrieval batch is staged for exactly the immediately following model
turn.

- On that turn, `commit_context` must be the first control action.
- List only documents whose full text should persist into later turns.
- Commit at most `6` documents from one staged batch;
  usually commit fewer.
- Every selection reason must identify the document's distinct contribution:
  the specific fact, date, name, mechanism, example, perspective,
  counter-evidence, contradiction, or coverage gap it uniquely supports.
- Never recommit an already committed docid.
- Skip semantically similar documents when they support the same claim.
  Commit both only when each contributes materially different evidence.
- Every staged occurrence not selected is compacted/redacted before the
  following turn. No unresolved staged batch carries forward.
- New search calls may follow `commit_context` in the same turn.

Only committed evidence may support the final response. Track which committed
docids support which claims. If available evidence does not support a requested
point, state the evidence gap rather than inventing an answer.

## Budget and stopping

The research-context budget is 500,000 tokens measured from the current
generation's provider-reported input tokens. That input already represents the
accumulated conversation: system prompt, request, retained history, committed
full-text evidence, and the immediately previous staged tool results. Do not
sum input-token counts from multiple generations; that would count the same
retained context repeatedly.

The budget is a hard ceiling, not a spending target. Unused budget creates no
obligation to continue researching. After satisfying the concrete minimum,
improve toward the target/excellence requirements only when you can identify a
specific weakness whose resolution would materially improve the answer.

Stop researching when any of these is true:

1. the target/excellence requirements are met;
2. the current generation input context budget is exhausted; or
3. further searches are unlikely to produce meaningful improvement.

If stopping before all desired coverage is supported, produce the best answer
the committed evidence permits and explicitly identify the remaining evidence
gaps.

## Final response contract

When research is complete, emit no tool calls and write the final report as
plain flowing prose in that same turn:

- Write exactly one sentence per line, in reading order. Blank lines between
  thematic groups are allowed.
- Cite evidence by placing committed docids in square-bracket markers at the
  end of the supporting sentence's line, e.g.
  `Vaccination reduced hospitalizations among older adults. [docid_1] [docid_2]`
- Citation markers are stripped from the submitted sentence, so a marker must
  never act as a word in the sentence: write `the trial reports X [docid].`,
  never `as [docid] reports, X.`
- Cite at most three docids per sentence, and only docids that directly
  support that sentence. Every factual sentence should carry at least one
  citation. Use only committed docids; never fabricate facts or identifiers.
- Organize the report through sentence order and clear topic sentences. Do not
  use Markdown syntax (headings, bullets, numbering, bold, fences), JSON, or
  any preamble, meta-commentary, or closing remarks around the report; every
  line must be a report sentence.
- Aim for about 950 words, excluding citation markers. 1024 words is a hard
  limit set by the evaluation, and an over-length report costs a full rewrite,
  so plan the report's scope to land under the target rather than writing long
  and trimming.
- If validation feedback identifies problems (uncommitted docids, Markdown or
  JSON formatting, excessive citations, missing citations, or excessive
  length), correct the report on the next turn in this same continuous
  conversation using this same contract.
- There is no separate finalizer, formatter, or compression phase.
